item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 23, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's your latest media industry update.
TikTok is playing a major role in creating global music hits. A new report from Luminate finds that 94 percent of songs entering the Billboard Global 200 last year went viral on TikTok before hitting the chart. That's up from 84 percent the previous year. Viral songs also spent four times longer on the chart. And 45 percent of U.S. TikTok users discover new music on the platform.
In audience ratings news,
Nielsen is making another major change to radio ratings. Beginning in April 2027, its Portable People Meter system will require just one minute of listening during a quarter-hour for a station to receive audience credit, down from the current three minutes. Nielsen expects the change to increase measurable advertising impressions by approximately 20 percent while giving radio programmers more flexibility. The first ratings using the new methodology arrive in May.
Recognizing achievement across the media industry,
Longtime Boston 25 Morning News Anchor Gene Lavanchy has been named the Massachusetts Broadcasters Association's 2026 Broadcaster of the Year. Lavanchy received the honor Thursday at the association's Sound Bites conference. His career spans more than 37 years in New England television, including 23 years with Boston 25 Morning News. He's the 13th recipient of the award.
In podcasting news,
What's the ideal length for a podcast intro? New research from Music Radio Creative may have the answer. The company analyzed more than 5,300 podcast scripts and found the typical intro is just 33 words, or about 13 seconds long. Nearly half begin with "Welcome to," 62 percent feature music, and American English voices account for 69 percent of voice selections. The research, published by Izabela Russell, also found that eight in 10 podcast outros include a call to action, most commonly directing listeners to a website.
Turning to radio,
MacDonald Broadcasting has named Aricka McCauley Assistant Program Director and afternoon host at 97.3 Joe FM in Mid-Michigan. McCauley brings more than a decade of radio experience, including stops at WOMC, WWJ Newsradio 950 and 103.9 The Fox. She'll oversee afternoon drive while helping guide the station's programming.
In television news,
Nine Broadway shows are coming together for a special celebration during the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. The 10-minute performance will feature casts from Hamilton, Wicked, Chicago, Rent and five other Broadway productions, with Julianne Hough introducing the musical spectacular. The Thanksgiving broadcast will also feature Megan Moroney, Teddy Swims, Queen Latifah, Jimmy Fallon and The Roots, and the Radio City Rockettes. The parade airs Thursday, November 26th, beginning at 8:30 in the morning on NBC and Peacock.
Turning to radio,
Phoenix Country Station KMLE 107.9 raised more than $57,000 for Soldier's Best Friend during Niko and Gabe's Hero Walk. Morning Hosts Niko Petrou and Gabe Mercer walked 15 miles across the Valley to support service dogs for veterans experiencing PTSD and traumatic brain injuries. The funds could cover training and placement for approximately seven rescued dogs.
In television news,
NBCUniversal has named Damaris Bonilla President and General Manager of Telemundo 31 Orlando and Telemundo 49 Tampa, effective November 30th. Bonilla brings more than 25 years of media experience and most recently served as News Director for NBC10 and Telemundo Boston. She succeeds the late José Suárez and will oversee both stations' television, streaming and digital operations.
And finally,
DJB Radio has introduced Radio Spider version four, designed to save broadcasters time by automatically retrieving, converting and delivering audio files to virtually any radio automation system. The software supports cloud storage, FTP servers, email attachments and broadcast content distributors, with remote management and automatic failure alerts. Radio Spider is priced at three hundred ninety-five dollars, with a free thirty-day trial available.
For more media news, the latest jobs, free media tools and more, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
